display.text: A standardized mean difference. This unit defines the one-sample version as d = (x̄ − μ₀)/s; benchmarks of about 0.2, 0.5, and 0.8 describe small, medium, and large magnitudes, subject to context.
A numerical measure of the magnitude of a difference or relationship, complementing a p-value by describing how large the observed effect is.
A test with a less-than alternative, whose z-test p-value is P(Z ≤ z_observed) under the standard normal null distribution.
The sampling distribution of a test statistic assuming H₀ is true. It supplies the reference probabilities used to calculate the p-value.
The specified population parameter value in H₀, written μ₀ for a mean or p₀ for a proportion; it is distinct from the observed sample statistic.
A large-sample test of H₀: p = p₀ using z = (p̂ − p₀)/√[p₀(1 − p₀)/n], with appropriate random sampling and at least ten expected successes and failures under H₀.
A test of H₀: μ = μ₀ using z = (x̄ − μ₀)/(σ/√n), with known population SD σ, suitable random sampling, and a normal or adequately approximated normal sampling distribution of x̄.

response.correctResponse: one-sample z-test for a population mean

display.text: An alternative hypothesis specifying a departure in one direction, such as μ > μ₀ or p < p₀. Its direction is determined by the research question before inspecting the result. Also called one-tailed alternative.
The substantive importance of an effect in its research context, considered using its size and plausible values rather than statistical significance alone.
A test with a greater-than alternative, whose z-test p-value is P(Z ≥ z_observed) under the standard normal null distribution.
The sampling spread calculated assuming H₀. For a proportion test it is √[p₀(1 − p₀)/n], using p₀ rather than p̂; for a mean with known σ it is σ/√n.

response.correctResponse: standard error under the null hypothesis

display.text: An alternative hypothesis allowing departure on either side of the null value, such as μ ≠ μ₀ or p ≠ p₀. Also called two-tailed alternative.
A test assessing departures in either direction. For a symmetric standard normal null distribution, its p-value is P(Z ≤ −|z|) + P(Z ≥ |z|).
The difference between a sample estimate and the null value divided by its standard error under H₀. Its sign indicates direction and its magnitude measures distance in standard-error units.
